Title: Diagnosis

Details:
The bug report states that while unpacking a CPIO archive, an EOFException (end-of-file exception) is thrown unexpectedly. The test case `testCpioUnarchive` creates a CPIO archive with two files, writes them to a file, then opens the CPIO archive for reading and extracts entries one by one.

Inspecting the code, the key method in reading entries is `CpioArchiveInputStream.getNextEntry()`, which delegates to `getNextCPIOEntry()`. This method reads the magic bytes at the start of each entry using `readFully`. The `readFully` method attempts to read a fixed number of bytes from the input stream and throws an EOFException if the end of the stream is encountered before the requested bytes are read.

The unexpected EOF likely happens because `readFully` expects to read the magic bytes of a next entry, but the stream has already ended. This can occur if the archive data ends before another entry header is found, or if the trailing data after the last entry is improperly handled.

The `getNextCPIOEntry()` method handles the special entry named "TRAILER!!!" as the end marker for the archive, returning null when it encounters this entry name and marking `entryEOF` as true. Thus, the unpacker relies on this trailer entry to know there are no more entries.

If the archive was created or read from a source missing the proper trailer entry or if the input stream was prematurely closed or truncated, `readFully` would throw EOFException trying to read the magic for the next entry.

Therefore, the root cause is that the CPIO input stream's `getNextCPIOEntry()` does not gracefully handle the premature end of stream before encountering the trailer entry, leading to an unexpected EOFException.

This aligns with the bug report referencing archives created by the compress classes or OSX command line where this issue manifests.

The failure is not triggered by the tested code per se, but by incomplete or corrupted data or a missing trailer entry in the input causing `readFully` to throw EOFException during header reading.

To fix the issue, `getNextCPIOEntry()` or `readFully()` should handle EOF more gracefully in the context of reading entries at the end of the archive to avoid throwing an exception when the stream simply ended.

Suggested fix locations will address handling EOF to return null or an appropriate indication instead of throwing.

---

Next, I will suggest which methods are best to fix the issue.
org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.cpio.CpioArchiveInputStream.getNextCPIOEntry()
org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.cpio.CpioArchiveInputStream.readFully(byte[],int,int)
